I could include "description": "An electromagnetic water meter". I'll set module_designation: null... Actually including null is acceptable. I'll include description instead.

Components: The cert names sub-assemblies: measuring sensor (FLC-2300 reduced bore / FLC-2200EL full bore) and electronic converter (FLC-406M, FLC-406AM). These are components. Record:
- role: "measuring sensor", type_designations: ["FLC-2300", "FLC-2200EL"], characteristics: bore reduced vs full
- role: "electronic converter (calculating and indicating device)", type_designations: ["FLC-406M", "FLC-406AM"], alternatives OR? The type is "with electronic converter FLC-406M and FLC-406AM" — both converters may be used with either type? It says "FLC-2300 and FLC-2200EL with electronic converter FLC-406M and FLC-406AM" — likely either converter. I'd say alternatives "OR" is plausible but not explicit. Hmm. Table 1 mentions "E1 for remote version of converter FLC-406M; E2 for compact version of converter FLC-406M; E2 for compact and remote version of converter FLC-406AM" — both converters exist in various versions. I'll record alternatives: "OR"? The wording "with electronic converter FLC-406M and FLC-406AM" suggests the type includes both converter options — i.e., OR. I'll set alternatives: "OR" for converters. Actually to avoid fabricating, I could set alternatives null. But rule 6 says when cert offers alternatives record "OR". The phrase lists both as part of type; typical reading: either converter can be fitted. I'll use "OR".

Also power supply: replaceable battery (2.9–3.7 V) or DC mains (10–28 V) only for FLC-406AM. That's a config-level characteristic (power supply type axis).

Model family: The cert covers family of instruments: two types × 9 meter sizes each. How to model? The model axis: two families — Table 2 reduced bore FLC-2300 with sizes DN50...DN300; Table 3 full bore FLC-2200EL with sizes DN50...DN300.

Model IDs: e.g. "FLC-2300 DN50", ... "FLC-2200EL DN300". That gives 18 models.

Then model_level characteristics: q1, q2, q3, q4, q3_q1_ratio, diameter_inlet_outlet (mm), accuracy class (per type), pressure loss class, verification scale interval (per size), indicating range.

Hmm, indicating device characteristics vary by size group — could be config_level with axis "meter size" and conditions like "DN50", "DN65-DN150". Or model_level per model. Let me put verification_scale_interval as model_level per model (18 models each), and indicating_range_minimum_value as type_level since it's same for all (9999999 m³). Verification scale interval varies: model_level attribute "maximum_verification_scale_interval", unit "m³", values per model.

Accuracy class: per type (model_level? config_level?). FLC-2200EL class 2, FLC-2300 class 1. Since models are "FLC-2300 DNxx", accuracy class per model could be model_level. But that's derived. config_level: [{attribute: "accuracy_class", axis: "meter type", values: [{condition: "FLC-2300", value: 1}, {condition: "FLC-2200EL", value: 2}]}]

- FLC-2300 based on doc 11690/0-06: Δp 10 for sizes < DN80; Δp 40 for sizes ≥ DN80
- FLC-2300 based on doc 11690/0-05: Δp 25 for sizes < DN80; Δp 40 for sizes ≥ DN80

I could record these as matrix_tables? Or config_level with two axes (documentation revision × size condition). config_level supports one axis per entry; I can emit multiple config_level entries:

- attribute: "pressure_loss_class", axis: "meter type", values: [{condition: "FLC-2200EL (all sizes)", value: "Δp 10", ...}]
- attribute: "pressure_loss_class", axis: "documentation 11690/0-06, meter size", values: [{condition: "FLC-2300, size < DN80", value: "Δp 10"}, {condition: "FLC-2300, size ≥ DN80", value: "Δp 40"}]
- attribute: "pressure_loss_class", axis: "documentation 11690/0-05, meter size", values: [{condition: "FLC-2300, size < DN80", value: "Δp 25"}, {condition: "FLC-2300, size ≥ DN80", value: "Δp 40"}]

Values as structured objects: {value: "Δp 10 (0.010 MPa or 0.10 bar)"} — value could be string "Δp 10", with note. The rule about footnote markers etc. I can include unit info in string. Let me structure: {"condition": "FLC-2300, size < DN80 (doc 11690/0-06)", "value": {"value": 10, "unit_symbol": "MPa"?}... Hmm pressure loss class Δp10 means max pressure loss 0.010 MPa. The class label itself is "Δp 10". I'll keep value as string "Δp 10" and maybe an accompanying numeric. Simpler: value: "Δp 10 (0.010 MPa / 0.10 bar)". But rule says values must be structured objects... For config_level, the example in rule 5: values follow same structured form: {condition, value, unit_symbol}. So {condition: "...", value: "Δp 10", unit_symbol: null}? The value inside should be the structured shape: the schema shows config_level values as {condition, value}. Given strictness "Every characteristic value MUST be an object with this shape" — shape {value, unit_symbol, unit_id, footnote_markers}. So config entries: {condition: "FLC-2200EL, all sizes", value: "Δp 10", unit_symbol: null}. Hmm but then "value" is a string "Δp 10" — fine, formulas/symbols keep as string.

Alternatively, treat max pressure loss numerically: attribute "maximum_pressure_loss", values: {value: 0.010, unit_symbol: "MPa"}. That's nicer. But class naming is Δp. I'll do pressure_loss_class with string values, and maybe include the MPa in parentheses within the string. Keep simple.

Environmental class: M1 / O (installed outdoors) — type_level: environmental_class: "M1 / O" — value string. Keep as string "M1 / O (installed outdoors)"? The class is M1/O; the parenthetical is a note. I'll put value "M1 / O" and maybe footnote? No footnote. I'll do value: "M1/O", and separate? Simpler: value: "M1 / O (installed outdoors)". I'll do just the MPa one plus maybe include parenthetical in a second key. I'll include both as separate canonical labels: maximum_admissible_pressure and maximum_admissible_pressure_equivalent. Fine.
